reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Rebuilt the credit counts, four choices and part-time placement from the Annex 1 matrix, then cross-checked Article 9.1 and the exact preparation, methods and thesis entries. Compared the substantive content of the VU interpretation and community study modules to the strongest current UCR courses and reviewed the final content fields and both feasible internal plans.
findings: Annex 1 has 10 taught components in each of stages 1 and 2 and five in stage 3, each worth 6 EC, plus 30 EC of genuine open study. Four stage-two choice slots use first-listed alternatives (G_BATRSAL084, G_BATRSAL054, G_BATRSPC219, G_BATRSPC207). Article 12.1 permits an approved minor, academic courses including at least 12 EC at level 300, or placement up to 12 EC and 18 EC courses. Article 10.4 puts the diagnostic Dutch test inside World Philosophy and specifies mainly Dutch instruction in the first two stages, then English in this route’s third stage.

Article 9.1 and the exact preparation, analytic methodologies and thesis entries agree. Preparation follows 120 EC including all first-year courses and first-semester second-year courses. The methods lab follows participation in preparation. The thesis follows passing preparation. The part-time sequence has those entry credits before the lab and schedules the two labs before the 6 EC thesis.

Annex 1 and exact entries distinguish cross-cultural myth and ritual, sacred interpretation and dialogue across religious traditions, religion-specific social theory, study of religious communities and religious ethics. The thesis explicitly studies a problem or phenomenon in theology or religious studies. The World Philosophy entry supports a partial philosophy correspondence, while generic literary interpretation and social research do not implement the full religion-specific functions.

Western Art History, spiritual self-fashioning in Life & Travel Writing, and Indigenous history strengthen the interdisciplinary plan. Their specific contributions, including artistic religious context and interpretive methods, still do not establish the defining progression in religious traditions, sacred texts and lived religion. The decision is based on academic comparability; both schedules pass availability and formal prerequisites.
